auth.register.title: Register a new account
auth.register.description:
Creates a new user account. The username is globally unique and the password is stored as a BCrypt hash. Returns the new user id.

common.captcha.title: Get a CAPTCHA image
common.captcha.description: Generates a 4-character CAPTCHA (SVG returned as a data URI usable directly as <img src>) with its captchaId and expiry. Stored in Redis; expires after 2 minutes and is consumed on the first verification attempt regardless of outcome, preventing replay brute force. Required before logging in (shared by user and admin sign-in).
auth.login.title: Log in
auth.login.description:
Validates the CAPTCHA and credentials, then issues a session token (valid for 7 days; JWT + Redis dual-track session: JWT carries the signature, Redis tracks active sessions so logout/forced sign-out revokes immediately). The CAPTCHA is verified first and consumed on use (single attempt). Wrong username and wrong password return the same error code to prevent account enumeration.

common.logout.title: Log out (user/admin shared)
common.logout.description:
Revokes the session of the current token; the token becomes invalid immediately after the call (send {} as the body). Works for both user and admin tokens: the session track is derived automatically from the token's token_kind claim.

common.logout_all.title: Force sign-out (all devices, user/admin shared)
common.logout_all.description:
Revokes all sessions of the current account in its own session track (user/admin, derived from the token's token_kind) across devices (use after password change or suspected account compromise) and returns the number of revoked sessions; the caller's own token is revoked as well (send {} as the body).

common.whoami.title: Who am I (user/admin shared)
common.whoami.description:
Returns the caller's identity: whether authenticated, subject id (user id or admin id), authentication scheme, display name and role list. Works for both user and admin tokens: admins always carry the admin role, super admins additionally have admin.super and llm.admin, so the front end can show/hide admin entry points. Requires a Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer <token>).

admin.login.title: Admin sign-in
admin.login.description:
Validates the CAPTCHA and admin credentials (separate AdminUsers table, no registration), then issues an admin session token (valid for 7 days; JWT + Redis dual-track session with immediate revocation). Regular admins carry the admin role; super admins additionally carry admin.super and llm.admin (they can provision accounts and manage model configs). Disabled accounts are rejected. The CAPTCHA is shared with GET /common:captcha, verified first and consumed on use. Use the shared endpoints common.logout / common.logout-all / common.whoami for admin sessions too (admin tokens work directly).

admin.setstatus.title: Enable or disable an admin account
admin.setstatus.description:
Enables or disables an admin account: disabled accounts cannot sign in and all their existing sessions are revoked immediately; disabling the currently signed-in account is rejected (accidental self-lockout). Super admin permission required.

admin.deleteuser.description:

openapi.tags.ai.name: AI Chat
openapi.tags.ai.description: LLM Q&A (requires sign-in; model credentials stored in database, isolated per tenant)

openapi.tags.prompt.name: Prompt Management
openapi.tags.prompt.description: Prompts are decoupled from model configs: one model can switch prompts per call (requires llm.admin permission)
ai.chat.description:
Sends a question to the LLM configured in the database and returns the answer with token usage. Falls back to the 'default' config when no alias is given. Prompts are decoupled from model configs: pass promptAlias to load that prompt (per tenant, from the Prompts table, effective immediately) as the system message; omit it to use the model config's default system prompt (if configured); model config is resolved per tenant + alias, keys are encrypted at rest and never written to config files.

ai.chat.title: Model chat (single-turn Q&A)
ai.chat.description:
Sends a question to the LLM configured in the database and returns the answer with token usage. llm.upsertconfig.title: Create or update a model configuration
llm.upsertconfig.description:
Creates or overwrites one model configuration: endpoint and model name are stored, the API key is encrypted with Data Protection before storage (listed masked); an optional system prompt (systemPrompt, ≤4000 chars) is prepended as a system message on chat. Omitting ApiKey / SystemPrompt on update keeps the existing values; an empty SystemPrompt clears it; on success the client cache is invalidated immediately so the next chat uses the new config without a restart.

llm.testconfig.title: Test model connectivity
llm.testconfig.description:
Sends a minimal request (ping) to the model using the saved config and returns success, latency and a truncated model reply. Diagnostic only — nothing is written, the key is never echoed; upstream errors return only the first line to avoid leaking sensitive data.

openapi.schemas.problem_details.descript: Returned on failure as RFC 9457 ProblemDetails. Clients should rely only on code to identify the error type, never parse detail text.
openapi.schemas.problem_details.properti: Error code in <domain>_<kind>_<number> form, e.g. AUTH_CONFLICT_001. Clients use it to identify the error type
HTTP status code mapped from the error kind (VALIDATION 400 / CONFLICT 409 / DENIED 403 / NOTFOUND 404 / UNEXPECTED 500)
Error kind, i.e. the KIND segment of the code (VALIDATION / CONFLICT / DENIED etc.)
Human-readable message localized to the caller's language (Accept-Language negotiation)
Trace id of this invocation, for log correlation
Field-level validation errors, present only for VALIDATION. Keys are field paths (dot-separated, e.g. lines[0].sku), values are message arrays
Extra scalar details attached to the error (e.g. retryAfter, id); collections and objects are not emitted
